security_audit.summary: The skill is documentation-heavy and does not contain prompt injection. It includes legitimate Claude API examples, links to external resources, local environment-variable guidance, a curl-to-shell installer command in contributor setup instructions, and a memory-tool example with bounded directory deletion. Publication should require warning/review for the installer and deletion examples, but no embedded secrets or malicious behavior were found.

remediation.issue: Contributor setup recommends piping a remote installer directly to sh.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the curl-to-shell shortcut with safer installation options or add checksum/signature verification and an explicit warning before execution.

remediation.issue: Examples show .env creation and API-key configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the environment-variable pattern, but explicitly remind users never to commit .env files or real API keys.

remediation.issue: The memory-tool example includes recursive directory deletion helpers.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the path validation safeguards and document that destructive memory operations should require user confirmation in production integrations.

content.value_statement: A curated Claude API cookbook that helps developers find practical examples for tool use, RAG, multimodal workflows, agents, prompt caching, evaluations, and common integration patterns.
actual_capabilities: Summarizes the major Claude cookbook categories and where to find each reference guide.
Provides copyable Python snippets for basic Messages API, tool use, vision, and prompt caching patterns.
Points users to examples for classification, retrieval augmented generation, summarization, text-to-SQL, and evaluations.
Highlights multimodal use cases including image analysis, OCR, chart interpretation, and form extraction.
Documents third-party integration topics such as Pinecone, Voyage AI embeddings, Wikipedia, web pages, LlamaIndex, and Deepgram.
Includes contributor guidance for setting up the cookbook repository and validating notebooks.
limitations: This skill is a documentation index and example guide; it does not install dependencies or run cookbook notebooks by itself.
Several code snippets use older Claude model identifiers and should be checked against current Anthropic model documentation before production use.
Some linked examples depend on external services, API keys, or third-party accounts that are not bundled with the skill.
The references summarize cookbook locations rather than embedding every notebook in full.

use_cases.title: Plan a Claude API integration
use_cases.description: Find starting points for basic Messages API calls, tool schemas, prompt caching, and model-selection practices.

use_cases.title: Prototype a RAG workflow
use_cases.description: Use the capability and third-party integration references to locate examples for embeddings, vector search, reranking, and domain-aware answer generation.

use_cases.title: Build multimodal document processing
use_cases.description: Locate vision examples for image upload, OCR, form extraction, chart interpretation, and PowerPoint analysis.
use_cases.target_user: Teams automating document or image analysis

use_cases.title: Explore agentic patterns
use_cases.description: Use the agent workflow references to study prompt chaining, routing, orchestrator-worker patterns, sub-agents, and evaluator-optimizer loops.

prompt_templates.title: Find a cookbook example
prompt_templates.scenario: A user knows the capability they need but not which reference file to open.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Claude Cookbooks skill to find the best reference for implementing {capability}. Summarize the relevant cookbook section and point me to the example path.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt an API pattern
prompt_templates.scenario: A user wants to turn a cookbook snippet into project-specific guidance.
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the Claude Cookbooks examples, explain how to implement {feature} in a {language_or_framework} app. Note any API keys, external services, or validation steps required.

prompt_templates.title: Compare approaches
prompt_templates.scenario: A user is choosing between multiple Claude patterns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Based on the Claude Cookbooks references, compare {approach_a} and {approach_b} for {use_case}. Recommend one and list the main tradeoff.

output_examples.input: Where should I start if I want to add tool use to my Claude app?
output_examples.output: Start with references/tool_use.md for the tool schema pattern and examples like the customer service agent and calculator integration. The key steps are defining a JSON input schema, passing tools to messages.create, validating tool inputs and outputs, and preserving context across tool interactions.

output_examples.input: I need examples for RAG with Claude.
output: Review references/capabilities.md for the RAG guide and contextual embeddings overview.
Check references/third_party.md for Pinecone, Voyage AI embeddings, Wikipedia, web page, and LlamaIndex integration pointers.
Expect to provide your own documents, embedding service credentials, and vector database setup.

best_practices: Use environment variables for API keys and keep .env files out of version control.
Verify model names and API parameters against current Anthropic documentation before copying older examples into production.
Start from the narrow cookbook section that matches the task rather than reading every reference file.
Treat third-party integration examples as patterns that require service-specific credentials, error handling, and quota management.
Run notebook validation and formatting tools before contributing cookbook changes.
anti_patterns: Do not paste placeholder API keys or real secrets into source files.
Do not run curl-to-shell installer commands without understanding and verifying the downloaded script.
Do not assume the summarized references include all notebook implementation details.
Do not use outdated model identifiers from examples without checking current model availability.
Do not enable destructive memory or filesystem operations in production without strict path validation and user confirmation.

faq.question: Does this skill execute Claude cookbook code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides documentation, pointers, and snippets. Users still need to install dependencies, configure API keys, and run notebooks or code in their own environment.

faq.question: Is it safe to publish?
faq.answer: It is generally documentation-oriented, but it should be published with warnings because it contains a curl-to-shell installer command, .env/API-key setup guidance, and examples of recursive deletion in a memory-tool script.

faq.question: What topics are covered?
faq.answer: The references cover Claude API basics, tool use, RAG, summarization, classification, text-to-SQL, multimodal vision workflows, third-party integrations, agents, evaluations, and prompt caching.

faq.question: Are the code snippets current?
faq.answer: Some snippets use older model identifiers, so developers should verify model names and SDK usage against current Anthropic documentation before production use.
